init.description: Quick guide: 1) Forward direction: pick the board axis that points to the front, or 'From drive calibration'. 2) Park on truly level ground and press 'Save as level' (can be repeated anytime, only changes the level reference). 3) Drive calibration (only needed for 'From drive calibration'): press start, wait 2 s, accelerate straight 1 to 3 times and brake to a full stop, then press stop. The switch 'Active' is not needed for calibrating. Full guide: link 'Visit' on the device page.

user.title: Relays & inputs
user.description: On the VAN PI CORE the MCP23017 sits at 0x20 on I2C bus 1: GPA0-7 = inputs 1-8, GPB0-7 = relays 1-8.

data_description.invert_inputs: On means input pulled to ground (default for the VAN PI CORE).
data_description.keep_state: On: relays keep their state when Home Assistant restarts. Off: all relays are switched off on start.

names.title: Names
names.description: Names for relays and inputs. Names from the old mcp23017 component are pre-filled. Empty = 'Relais n' / 'Eingang n'.

error.not_found: No MCP23017 answers at this address.
error.already_configured: This address is already set up.

user.title: Tank
user.description: Tank input 1-4 of the VAN PI CORE. The sensor type switches the board pull-up for the channel pair 1+2 or 3+4, so both channels of a pair need the same sensor type. The curve converts the measured voltage into the level.

data_description.curve: Pairs voltage:level separated by comma, e.g. 0:0, 0.49:50, 1.6:100. Below the first / above the last point the end value is used.
data_description.divider_ratio: 1 if the sensor is connected directly.
data_description.r_pullup_ohm: Only for resistive sensors (about 47 kΩ on the board).
data_description.mode: Voltage: sender with its own output voltage, e.g. a capacitive Votronic probe (about 0-2.4 V) or a rod probe with resistor board. Resistive: classic float/lever sender to ground.

error.already_configured: This channel is already set up.
error.pair_conflict: Channels 1+2 and 3+4 share one pull-up. The other channel of this pair already uses the other sensor type.
